name: Nangibotide
status: Investigational; phase 2 trials done; FDA-agreed phase 3 design announced Jan 2024; not approved
mechanism: A 12-amino-acid decoy peptide that traps the ligand of TREM-1, an immune-cell receptor that amplifies inflammation in septic shock

article.summary: Nangibotide is an experimental peptide that dampens TREM-1, an inflammation amplifier, in septic shock. Its phase 2b trial missed the main goal; a biomarker-guided phase 3 has been planned.
article.takeaway: Nangibotide is a 12-amino-acid peptide that acts as a decoy for the ligand of TREM-1, a receptor on immune cells that amplifies inflammation and is switched on in septic shock.[^1] In the 355-patient phase 2b ASTONISH trial it did **not** meet its main goal, a change in organ-failure score (SOFA) by day 5, in the pre-set high-sTREM-1 group or overall, although higher sTREM-1 cutoffs hinted at a benefit that needs confirming.[^2] A phase 2 trial in 220 patients with COVID-19 reported better day-28 clinical status and lower mortality, but it was stopped early.[^3] In January 2024 the developer said the FDA had agreed the design of a single phase 3 trial.[^4] It is not FDA-approved.
glance: Continuous IV infusion in intensive care trials
Three randomized phase 2 trials (49, 355 and 220 patients)

blocks.text: TREM-1 is a receptor on infection-fighting cells. When it is activated it drives out inflammatory chemicals and boosts its own production, and a cleaved piece of it, soluble TREM-1 (sTREM-1), circulates in the blood. People with sepsis and septic shock have raised sTREM-1, which is why researchers see TREM-1 as a driver of the runaway immune response.[^1]

Nangibotide, also called LR12, is a chemically made 12-amino-acid fragment derived from a related protein, TLT-1. It acts as a ligand-trapping decoy, meant to turn down TREM-1-driven amplification without shutting off the immune system altogether.[^1] As of a 2024 review, it was the only TREM-1 inhibitor to have entered clinical trials.
Inotrem, a French company, has run three randomized phase 2 trials: a 49-patient phase 2a and the 355-patient ASTONISH phase 2b in septic shock, plus a 220-patient trial in COVID-19.[^5][^2][^3]

In January 2024 the company announced that, after end-of-phase-2 talks, the FDA had agreed the design of one phase 3 registration trial, ACCURATE: about 1,300 patients (900 in the primary analysis) with high sTREM-1, about 100 sites, and a primary endpoint of being alive and free of organ support at day 29. A Roche sTREM-1 blood test is planned as the companion diagnostic.[^4] ClinicalTrials.gov lists no phase 3 nangibotide trial as of this writing.

rows: 49 patients with septic shock; three doses or placebo for up to 5 days
No significant increase in adverse events; no anti-drug antibodies; SOFA changes favored nangibotide but were not significant[^5]
Main SOFA goal not met; day-28 mortality overall 25% placebo, 32% low dose, 25% high dose; a benefit signal only at higher sTREM-1 cutoffs[^2]
220 patients with COVID-19 on respiratory support; stopped early
Clinical status improved by day 28 in 64.7% vs 52.0% (odds ratio 1.79); day-28 mortality 16.0% vs 28.0%[^3]

blocks.text: The COVID-19 trial stopped after 220 patients, so its encouraging findings are not definitive.

In ASTONISH, treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 95-96% of patients in every arm and serious ones in 22-26%, typical for septic shock and similar across groups.[^2] The phase 2a trial found no anti-drug antibodies.[^5] Long-term and real-world safety are unknown, and the peptide has only been given in intensive care trials.

Phase 3 aims to treat only septic shock patients with high sTREM-1, a precision approach that needs the blood test to be validated alongside the drug.[^4] Because the phase 2b trial missed its primary goal, success is uncertain. A positive, larger trial would be required before any approval.

evidence.label: Early: three phase 2 trials with mixed results
evidence.text: About 620 patients in total have been randomized across three phase 2 trials, with the main goal missed in septic shock and a more positive signal in COVID-19.[^2][^3] Efficacy is unproven until a phase 3 trial reports.

faq.q: What is sTREM-1 and why does it matter?
faq.a: sTREM-1 is a fragment of the TREM-1 receptor shed into the blood during inflammation. Higher levels mark more TREM-1 activation, and the trials used it to try to pick patients more likely to benefit.[^1][^2]
No. It is investigational and has been given only in clinical trials.

faq.q: Did the trials show it saves lives?
faq.a: Not in septic shock: ASTONISH missed its main goal and showed no overall mortality benefit,[^2] while the COVID-19 trial reported lower day-28 mortality but stopped early.[^3]
